_about: Artefact register for the paper. Every md5 and byte count here was MEASURED by hashing the file on 2026-11-01, and every s3 key was checked with `aws s3 ls --profile race-wm --recursive` on its prefix. A number in a document is a claim; this file records what the files actually are. Checkpoints and datasets are gitignored, so md5 -- not filename -- is what matches a stray .pt to a run.

_s3.access: private bucket; a reader outside the project cannot fetch these without credentials

_obtainable_legend.s3-private: in the private S3 bucket; recoverable by anyone with the race-wm profile
_obtainable_legend.local-only: exists only on this Mac. NOT recoverable if the machine is lost -- these are the rows that need an upload
_obtainable_legend.gone: neither local nor in S3; the reason is in missing_reason

_byte_identical_note: Two registered names hashing the same means one file is serving two roles. checkpoints/kept/rvs_anchor.pt.last.pt == checkpoints/kept/rvs_from_v15.pt is the one that matters: the local copy of the gohma-rvs2-anchor result (PROVENANCE 15) is byte-identical to the UNTRAINED v15-widened init, so these weights do not demonstrate the anchor run's training. The pod-side checkpoint, not this file, is what PROVENANCE 15 means.
